notes: The variable Akter & Grafton used (15+ unpaid hours, women vs men). 2021 from https://www.abs.gov.au/census/find-census-data/datapacks; ABS summary https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/people-and-communities/unpaid-work-and-care-census/latest-release. Single before/after pair only.

dataset: Quarterly recorded crime dataset by Suburb (62 offences incl. domestic violence related assault; monthly counts)
approx_size: SuburbData.zip (https://www.bocsar.nsw.gov.au/Documents/Datasets/SuburbData.zip); size not stated, likely tens of MB
notes: Domestic assault is one offence. Suburb/postcode counts are small, so pool areas and use multi-month windows. Resource page returned 403 on direct read; details come from search summaries.

dataset: Quarterly recorded crime dataset by LGA (RCI_offencebymonth.xlsm)
notes: Fallback if suburb counts are too small.

dataset: NSW Crime Tool (maps and summaries by LGA, suburb, postcode)
notes: Viewing only. Domestic violence is under-reported and fires can cut reporting or policing access.

dataset: NSW government school enrolments by head count (by school)
publisher: NSW Department of Education via data.nsw.gov.au
notes: Enrolment change by school near fires shows displacement. School locations can be joined to fire footprints.

dataset: Attendance rate at government schools, NSW
notes: Too coarse and too recent; does not cover Black Summer.

dataset: ACARA My School and Data Access Program (school-level attendance, NAPLAN, enrolment)
notes: Per-school extract needs an application.

dataset: School closure days during bushfires
notes: Only totals found (about 600 schools closed late 2019; 250+ directly affected); no school-by-day list public.

dataset: ACARA My School NAPLAN results by school (extract via Data Access Program)
approx_size: extract by request; My School website free to view
notes: Gibbs et al. found lower gains at 2 and 4 years in high-impact Black Saturday schools. A Black Summer test compares gains in schools near footprints with similar schools; 2020 NAPLAN cancelled and covid confounds.

dataset: NSW government school enrolments by head count
notes: Defines school population and fire proximity.

dataset: NSW Air Quality monitoring network data download and Data Explorer (PM2.5, PM10, ozone)
publisher: NSW Government (Climate Change, Energy, Environment and Water)
approx_size: CSV per station-year; multi-year all-station hourly likely tens to hundreds of MB
notes: Smoke exposure (X variable). Stations are sparse outside towns; assign each SA2 to nearest station.

dataset: HealthStats NSW: asthma and unplanned ED presentations (monthly)
notes: Outcome side at LHD scale only. Admissions by postcode/SA2 need NSW Health Admitted Patient data via request; see HealthStats Hospitalisations https://healthstats.nsw.gov.au/topic-overview//Hospitalisations

dataset: AIHW Medicare-subsidised GP, allied health, specialist use across local areas
notes: Annual GP and specialist use at SA3; too coarse for days-to-weeks smoke events.

dataset: NSW Valuer General Bulk Property Sales Information (PSI)
geography: individual property with address, postcode and LGA
time_step: weekly updates; each sale has a contract and settlement date
approx_size: zipped weekly and annual DAT files; total many GB, size not seen
notes: Free for non-commercial use (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0); commercial use needs a PSI licence. Fields include price, land size, postcode. This is the best fine-scale price source: daily sale dates, postcode or street level.

dataset: NSW Valuer General Bulk Land Value information
publisher: NSW Valuer General / Valuation Services Portal
time_step: annual valuing date (1 July) with monthly file refresh; up to 5 valuing years per file
approx_size: monthly zip of one CSV per LGA; size not shown
notes: CC BY 4.0. Land values are the council rate base, so this measures rateable value changes by council or property. Annual valuation limits timing.

dataset: ABS Total Value of Dwellings (mean price and number of dwellings)
geography: state and capital city / rest-of-state in the download; methodology uses SA2 but SA2 tables are not shown in the release page I fetched
years: series from 2021 on the page graph; latest June quarter 2026
notes: Too coarse for fire-matched tests. Included to show what not to rely on.

dataset: Building Approvals by Statistical Area (SA2 and above)
publisher: Australian Bureau of Statistics via data.gov.au
geography: SA2 for some historic series; current releases LGA, SA4, state
years: to current; SA2 available only for some past releases (e.g. 2017-18, 2019-20)
notes: Rebuilding activity as a rate-base proxy; useful monthly but SA2 coverage is limited, so LGA may be the practical level.

dataset: NSW Fair Trading Rental Bond Data (monthly postcode)
notes: Already used at council level in Experiment 7 (rents not detected). I did not re-verify this URL this session. Postcode-level monthly re-cut would be finer.

dataset: CoreLogic Home Value Index and sales (commercial)
notes: Paid; not recommended for a school project. Mentioned only because it is the standard property price source.

dataset: DRFA Activation History by LGA
notes: Count of declared disasters per LGA in the years before and after each fire (floods 2021-22, storms, COVID not included).

dataset: NSW declared natural disasters list
notes: Cross-check for the DRFA list; fetch returned 403 in my session.

dataset: NSW Rental Bond Lodgement (monthly by postcode)
notes: Page showed monthly files only from 2022, so older years come from the annual files or the data.nsw.gov.au series. Only a weak monthly stress signal.

dataset: Census 2021 DataPacks: industry of employment (accommodation and food, agriculture, forestry) by place of usual residence
notes: 2016 gives the pre-fire tourism employment share. Table number (G54) not confirmed in this session.

dataset: Census Place of Work (POWP) and Working Population by destination zone
approx_size: via TableBuilder or DataPack (size not confirmed)
notes: Counts jobs where the workplace is, which is better than where workers live for tourist towns. The DataPacks page I fetched did not list a Working Population pack, so TableBuilder is the safer route.

dataset: Tourism Research Australia LGA visitor and accommodation profiles (visitors, nights, spend)
publisher: Destination NSW with Tourism Research Australia
years: profiles from 2013; years per file not confirmed
notes: Survey-based, noisy for small LGAs. Good for tourism share of local spend.

dataset: FESM 2019-20 plus fire start dates (to place each fire in the Christmas peak or not)
notes: Fire month by council is already in the project's fire list; this adds severity.
